transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess… I’ve just noticed I’m not really enjoying the things that used to keep me steady. It’s not like everything’s falling apart or anything, but sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, even working out in the woodshop—lately they all feel more like chores I keep putting off. My family thought it might be good if I talked to someone, and… I suppose they’re probably right.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I’d say… a little over a year now. It kind of started after that scaffold accident, during the business readjustment. I didn’t really think much of it at first—I figured I’d bounce back—but it’s been lingering longer than I expected, if that makes sense.

Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or enjoyment in activities like sailing races or working out in the woodshop, or do you still find some satisfaction in them even if you're not getting to them as much?

Yeah… I mean, I wish I could say I still get the same satisfaction from them, but honestly that’s kind of what finally made me agree to come in. I just don’t seem to care about the things that used to keep me balanced.

The sailing races, the Saturday historical society shift, tinkering out in the woodshop… they all sort of feel like chores now. I keep putting them off. It’s not that I hate them or anything, I just… don’t feel pulled toward them the way I used to. Does that make sense?
Are there any activities at all that you still find enjoyable or look forward to, or does it feel like you’ve lost interest in pretty much everything?

I wouldn’t say it’s everything, exactly… I mean, I can still get through the day and there are little moments that are fine. But the bigger things I used to actually look forward to—sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, tinkering in the woodshop—those just don’t pull me in anymore.

They feel more like chores I keep putting off, which is… hard to admit, I guess. That’s really what finally made me agree to come in. I just don’t care about the things that used to keep me balanced, and I’m not sure if I’m explaining that right.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most days, even if you can't quite put your finger on why?

Yeah… I guess “depressed” sounds a little strong to me, maybe, but there is this kind of low-grade dread most days. And guilt, too.

It follows me around more than I’d like to admit—like I should’ve seen one more risk coming, even though people keep telling me the controls were in place. I know that may not be the same thing as being depressed, but… it’s there. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find that this low mood or dread is present most of the day, nearly every day, or does it come and go in a way that feels more occasional?

It’s… more present than occasional, I think. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I can still function and do what I’m supposed to do, but that low-grade dread and guilt is kind of there in the background most days.

It follows me around, like I should’ve seen one more risk coming, even though people keep telling me the controls were in place. Some moments are lighter than others, sure, but it doesn’t really feel like it just comes and goes completely. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite lately, or do you often feel tired even when you haven't done much physically?

Sleep, yeah… a bit. I don’t think my appetite’s changed much, not that I’ve noticed. But most nights I can get to bed at a reasonable time, so it’s not like I’m up all night on purpose.

It’s more that I wake up around two or three, and then my mind is right back on that job site. After that I’m just lying there, listening for every little sound, and it doesn’t feel like real rest. I still get up and do what I need to do, but… yeah, I guess I’m more tired than I should be. Does that count?
Do you often feel like you don’t have the energy to do things, or do you get tired more easily than before, even when you haven't done much?

I’m not sure I’d say I “don’t have energy,” exactly. I still get things done, and I don’t want to overstate it.

But… I do feel a little more worn out than I used to, maybe. Like things take more out of me, even if they’re not physically demanding. It’s not every minute, and I can push through, but I notice I’m not quite as refreshed as I should be. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel like you're not doing enough, or find yourself dwelling on thoughts that you're somehow responsible for things that went wrong, even when others tell you otherwise?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to sit there blaming myself outright, because I know that’s not really fair. People have told me the controls were in place and that I couldn’t have accounted for everything.

But there’s still this… low-grade guilt, I guess. This dread that follows me around, like maybe I should’ve seen one more risk coming. I keep going back over it in my head, wondering if I missed something I should’ve caught. I know that probably sounds like I’m second-guessing too much, but… yes, that’s there.
Have you had any periods of time where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks in a row, without them getting better for more than a few days?

Yeah… I think that’s probably part of why I finally agreed to come in, honestly.

I wouldn’t say I’m completely shut down or anything. I still show up for work, still handle what I’m supposed to. But the things that used to kind of keep me steady—sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, messing around in the woodshop—they just don’t pull me in the same way. They feel more like chores now, and I keep putting them off.

It’s been going on long enough that I can’t really say it’s just a bad couple of days. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yes, I guess I have noticed that.
Have you noticed your ability to work or carry out your usual responsibilities being affected by how you’ve been feeling?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m not functioning. I’m still doing my job, keeping up with the main responsibilities.

But I have noticed I’m… shifting things around more than I used to. Like site visits that I probably should be leading myself, I’ll delegate to someone else if I can. And if a client conversation is going to get near the accident, I tend to avoid being the one to handle it.

I tell myself that’s just practical, but… I do worry I’m not giving the project the steady direction it really needs. Does that answer what you mean?
